engines.t: **Mulcharmy Fuwalos** ×3 draws a card each time your opponent Special Summons from the Deck or Extra Deck. **Forbidden Droplet** ×2 negates their monsters, and **Super Polymerization** ×3 fuses them away. Ash Blossom ×3, Effect Veiler ×2, Ghost Ogre, Droll & Lock Bird and Nibiru interrupt their turn.

**Chaos Angel** (Level 10) banishes a card when Summoned. **Snake-Eyes Vengeance Dragon** (Level 12) turns a monster into a Continuous Spell on either turn. **Tri-Edge Master** draws a card when made with a Level 2 + a Level 4. **S:P Little Knight** banishes a card. The four Fusions are for Super Polymerization.

facts.t: **Witch of the White Forest** stops you Special Summoning DARK monsters from the Extra Deck for the rest of the turn it searches. That covers Chaos Angel, S:P Little Knight, TY-PHON, Garura and Starving Venom.
**Filia Diabell** only adds a Level 8 or higher Diabell monster: Diabellze or Diabellstar Vengeance. Diabellstar the Black Witch is Level 7, so WANTED is the card that finds her.
**Diabellstar Vengeance** needs 1 Spell **and** 1 Trap banished from your hand or GY. The deck runs only 2 Traps (Morrian and Curse of Diabell), so make sure one of them is reachable.
**Mulcharmy Fuwalos** can only be discarded while you control no cards. Going second, use it in their turn before you have anything on the field.

**Snake-Eyes Doomed Dragon** has no Snake-Eye material in this deck. Summon it the other way: Poplar places 2 White Forest monsters in your Spell & Trap Zone, and Doomed Dragon is Summoned by sending those 2 to the GY.

**Elzette, Azamina** has a Fusion effect with nothing to Summon here (no Azamina Fusion is run). She is played for her free Summon and for the Sinful Spoils card she adds when used as Synchro Material.

combos.h: Line A — Elzette into Diabell, Queen
combos.about: One Elzette becomes three Level 8s that protect each other. Elzette finds Silvy, Silvy finds the Field Spell Witch, and Witch finds a second Level 2. Silvy + that Level 2 make the Synchro Tuner Rciela, and Rciela + Elzette make the Queen. Along the way Rciela and Elzette Azamina fetch the Diabell cards, so Diabellze and Diabellstar Vengeance join for free.

combos.h: Line B — Diabellstar into Vengeance
combos.about: The line for hands without Elzette or Silvy, and it uses no Normal Summon. WANTED finds Diabellstar, who Summons herself by sending 1 card and Sets a Trap from your Deck. Diabellze sends that Trap to Summon herself, then puts Diabellstar Vengeance in the GY, and Vengeance Summons itself from there. Three witches protect each other, and Vengeance destroys a card on their turn.

steps.t: Activate WANTED: **add Diabellstar the Black Witch** from your Deck.
Send Forbidden Droplet (any card works) from your hand to the GY to **Special Summon Diabellstar**.
Diabellstar was Summoned: **Set Sinful Spoils of Slumber - Morrian** from your Deck.
Send the Set Morrian from your field to the GY to **Special Summon Diabellze** from your hand.

If you also hold Elzette, play this line first and use the Set Sinful Spoils card as her cost.

combos.about: **Super Polymerization** is a Quick-Play Spell: discard 1 card, then Fusion Summon using monsters from **either** field. Neither player can respond to it. Two of their best monsters (or one of theirs and one of yours) become one Fusion Monster on your side. The materials are sent to the GY without being targeted or destroyed, so their protection doesn't help. Pick the Fusion by what the two monsters share:

white-forest.pitch: A Synchro deck that pays for everything with Spells and Traps. Small Level 2 Spellcasters Summon themselves by sending a Spell/Trap to the GY, climb into LIGHT Synchro Monsters, and finish on **Diabell, Queen of the White Forest** with the Diabellstar witches beside her.

plan.first: Climb from Elzette or Silvy to **Diabell, Queen** with Diabellze and Diabellstar Vengeance next to her. On their turn the Queen Summons Silvera to flip their whole field face-down, and Vengeance destroys a card.
plan.second: Discard **Mulcharmy Fuwalos** while your field is empty to draw as they combo. On your turn, Forbidden Droplet and Super Polymerization take their board apart before you start your own plays.
plan.win: Three 2500+ ATK monsters that protect each other from destruction. Silvera turns their monsters face-down and gives your Synchros double piercing damage against them.

open.t: The best starter. Send 1 Spell/Trap to Summon her from your hand, and she adds Silvy.
Normal Summon her to add Witch of the White Forest, which then adds a Level 2.
Adds Diabellstar the Black Witch: a free Level 7 that Sets a Sinful Spoils card from your Deck.
A starter by itself: activating it adds Elzette or Silvy. It is also the Spell you most often send as a cost.

stops: **Ash Blossom on Elzette's or Silvy's search.** Keep going: make Rciela anyway, and her search replaces the card you lost.
**Witch's DARK lock.** After Witch searches, you can't Special Summon DARK monsters from the Extra Deck that turn (S:P Little Knight, Chaos Angel, Garura, Starving Venom, TY-PHON). Use those first.
**Running out of Spells/Traps.** Nearly every White Forest effect costs one. Count them before you start, and send the ones you need least.

horus-mitsurugi.pitch: Two engines that both make Level 8 monsters. The **Horus** monsters Summon themselves from the GY for free while King's Sarcophagus is on the field. The **Mitsurugi** Ritual Monsters wipe the opponent's monsters and make them pay for every effect. Any two Level 8s can then overlay into a Rank 8 Xyz Monster.

plan.first: Ritual Summon **Ame no Murakumo** and **Futsu no Mitama**, Set **Mitsurugi Great Purification**, and bring out Imsety + Hapi beside them. Each effect they activate meets Murakumo's "discard a card or it's negated".
plan.second: Murakumo destroys every monster they control when it is Special Summoned. Super Polymerization and Infinite Impermanence deal with whatever is left.
plan.win: After the wipe, Imsety + Hapi overlay into **Draglubion**, which Summons **Numeron Dragon** for a 9000 ATK attack. Going first, the Horus monsters keep coming back from the GY every turn.

**Losing King's Sarcophagus.** The Horus monsters only come back while it is face-up. Walls of the Imperial Tomb in the Field Zone is your second copy, so try to have both.
**Draglubion's lock.** After its effect you can't Special Summon anything else that turn and only the monster it Summoned can attack. Finish your Ritual plays first.

combos.h: Line A — Walls into Imsety + Hapi
combos.about: The Horus engine from one Field Spell and two spare cards, with no Normal Summon. Walls finds Imsety. Imsety sends itself to the GY to find the real King's Sarcophagus, and Sarcophagus sends Hapi from the Deck. Both then Summon themselves from the GY, because you control King's Sarcophagus.

steps.t: **Activate Walls of the Imperial Tomb** in your Field Zone. While it is there, its name is King's Sarcophagus.
Walls' effect: **add Imsety** from your Deck, then put 1 card from your hand (here Nibiru) on the bottom of your Deck.
Imsety's effect: send Imsety and 1 other card (here Droll & Lock Bird) from your hand to the GY. **Add King's Sarcophagus**, then draw 1.
You control "King's Sarcophagus" (Walls), so **Special Summon Imsety** from your GY.
Activate King's Sarcophagus. Send the card you drew from your hand to the GY, then **send Hapi** from your Deck to the GY.
**Special Summon Hapi** from your GY the same way.

end.t: Imsety + Hapi with both Sarcophagus cards. Effects that destroy without targeting can't destroy them. If their effect removes one of your other cards, Imsety sends 1 card on the field to the GY and Hapi returns 2 cards from the GYs or banishment. If they are destroyed anyway, they Summon themselves again next turn.

rules: Opening Imsety and no Walls? Start at step 3, then activate King's Sarcophagus and continue.
Imsety and Hapi can each Summon themselves from the GY once per turn.
King's Sarcophagus's send effect costs 1 card from your hand each time. A second Imsety in hand is a good card to send.

combos.h: Line B — Mitsurugi Ritual into Murakumo and Futsu
combos.about: Two Spells become both Ritual bosses and a Set negate. Mitsurugi Ritual pays for Murakumo by Tributing two Level 4s **from your Deck**, and each one searches because it was Tributed. Mitsurugi Mirror then Tributes Murakumo to Summon Futsu, and Murakumo searches and comes straight back.

steps.t: Activate Mitsurugi Prayers without Tributing: **add Ame no Murakumo** from your Deck.
Activate Mitsurugi Ritual, second effect: **Ritual Summon Murakumo** from your hand by Tributing Aramasa + Saji (Level 4 + 4) from your Deck.
Murakumo was Special Summoned: **destroy all monsters your opponent controls** (this is your board wipe when going second).
Aramasa was Tributed: **add Futsu no Mitama**. Saji was Tributed: **add Mitsurugi Mirror**.
Activate Mitsurugi Mirror: **Ritual Summon Futsu** from your hand by Tributing Murakumo (Level 8) from your field.
Murakumo was Tributed: **add Mitsurugi Great Purification**, then Murakumo Special Summons itself.
**Set Mitsurugi Great Purification.** You still have your Normal Summon.

end.t: Murakumo + Futsu with Great Purification Set. Each turn, the first time they activate something, Murakumo makes them discard 1 card or it is negated. When they Special Summon, Futsu revives Aramasa or Saji, which searches again. Great Purification Tributes Futsu to negate and destroy, and Futsu adds a card and returns.

rules: Mitsurugi Ritual has two effects, each once per turn. Only the one that Summons from your **hand** can Tribute from the Deck.
Each Murakumo effect is once per turn, so it doesn't wipe their field again when it comes back in step 6.
Only 1 Mitsurugi Prayers per turn. With a Mikoto in hand, Tribute it on activation to get both of Prayers' effects.

kashtira-maliss.pitch: A Link deck that banishes its own cards on purpose. Every **Maliss** monster does something when it is banished: most pay 300 LP and Special Summon themselves. One Maliss monster turns into a chain of free Summons that ends on **Hearts Crypter**, a Link-3 that banishes a card on either turn and can't be negated.

plan.first: Turn Dormouse or White Rabbit into **Red Ransom**, then **Hearts Crypter**, with Maliss in Underground on the field. On their turn Hearts Crypter banishes 1 card, and your hand traps do the rest.
plan.second: Special Summon **Kashtira Fenrir** on your empty field first, then run the Maliss line. Bystials, Infinite Impermanence and Nibiru break their board, and **Accesscode Talker** destroys what is left.
plan.win: Accesscode Talker at 5300 ATK plus Red Ransom, or Fenrir and Hearts Crypter banishing a card every turn until they run out.

Banish a Maliss card from your hand, then draw 2. Banished: pay 300 LP to Summon itself.
Quick Effect in hand: banish another Maliss card from your hand or GY to Summon it. Banished: pay 300 LP to add a banished Maliss monster to your hand.
Link-3. Summoned: adds a Maliss Spell. Banished: pay 900 LP to Summon it, then banish a Cyberse monster from your Deck.
Link-3. Quick Effect: shuffle 1 of your banished Maliss cards into the Deck and banish 1 card on the field. Can't be negated while it points to a monster.
Trap. Can be used the turn it is Set by banishing a Maliss monster you control. Special Summons a Maliss monster from your Deck.
Trap, same activation. Adds a Maliss monster, then banishes 1 card on the field if you control a Maliss Link.

engines.t: Level 7 monsters you Summon before anything else, because they need an empty field. They need no Normal Summon and they banish face-down, which almost nothing can recover.

key.t: Main Phase: adds a Kashtira monster. When it attacks, or when they activate a monster effect, banish 1 of their face-up cards face-down.
Same Summon. When it attacks, or when they activate a monster effect, look at their Extra Deck and banish 1 monster from it face-down.
Field Spell. Adds a Kashtira monster when activated. Shares the Field Zone with Maliss in Underground, so play it first.

engines.t: **Cynet Mining** ×3, **Gold Sarcophagus** and **Terraforming** (for Underground) all find your first Maliss monster. **Backup @Ignister** Summons itself once a Link is out and adds another. **Bystial Druiswurm and Magnamhut** banish a DARK monster from either GY to Summon themselves: banish your own Maliss monster and it triggers.

**Haggard Lizardose** banishes a Maliss monster from your GY. **Accesscode Talker** destroys a card for each Link you banish. **Underworld Goddess** uses 1 of their monsters as material. **S:P Little Knight** banishes a card. **Borrelend Dragon** and the two Topologics are big finishers. I:P Masquerena, Dharc, Selene, Cherubini, Almiraj and Linguriboh fill gaps.
cards: Underworld Goddess of the Closed World

facts.t: **Every Maliss monster effect is once per turn by name.** After Chessy Cat has Summoned itself from banishment once, a second Chessy Cat banished the same turn stays banished.
**Hearts Crypter needs exactly 3 monsters**, so a Link Monster counts as only 1 material for it. Red Ransom says "2+ monsters", so Haggard Lizardose (Link-2) + 1 monster is enough.
**Maliss in Underground's +3000 ATK never turns on here.** It needs 3 different Maliss Traps banished and the deck runs 2. Play it for the banish on activation and the attack redirect.
**Maliss Traps can be activated the turn they are Set** by banishing a face-up Maliss monster you control. That banish is a cost, and it triggers the monster.
**Bystials can banish your own monsters.** Druiswurm or Magnamhut banishing a Maliss monster from your GY Summons a Level 6 and triggers the Maliss.
**Cards with nothing to use here:** Kashtira Unicorn's Spell search (no Kashtira Spell is run), Wraitsoth's destroy effect (no Shangri-Ira), and Linguriboh's revival.

str: One Maliss monster is a full combo, and nine other cards find one.
Hearts Crypter's banish can't be negated while it points to a monster.
Kashtira gives a strong play that doesn't use the Normal Summon or the Maliss engine.
22 hand traps and going-second cards.
weak: A full combo costs about 2000 LP.
White Rabbit and Dormouse are 1 copy each (both Limited).
Maliss in Underground and Pressured Planet Wraitsoth share the Field Zone.
Cards that stop banishing or banished effects shut the engine off.

combos.h: Line A — Dormouse into Hearts Crypter
combos.about: One Normal Summon becomes two Link-3s. Dormouse banishes White Rabbit, and both keep Summoning themselves back while Haggard Lizardose and Red Ransom are built from them. Red Ransom finds Underground for a third monster. The Trap TB-11 then banishes Red Ransom as a cost, and Red Ransom simply returns, bringing March Hare with it.

steps.t: **Normal Summon Dormouse.** Its effect banishes White Rabbit from your Deck.
White Rabbit was banished: pay 300 LP to **Special Summon it**. When Summoned, it **Sets TB-11** from your Deck.
**Link Summon Haggard Lizardose** using Dormouse + White Rabbit.
Lizardose's effect: banish Dormouse from your GY (target Lizardose). Dormouse was banished: pay 300 LP to **Special Summon it**.
**Link Summon Red Ransom** using Lizardose + Dormouse. It adds Maliss in Underground from your Deck.
**Activate Underground**: banish Chessy Cat from your Deck. Chessy Cat was banished: pay 300 LP to Special Summon it.
**Activate the Set TB-11** by banishing Red Ransom from your field. TB-11 Special Summons a second Chessy Cat from your Deck.
Red Ransom was banished: pay 900 LP to **Special Summon it**, then banish March Hare from your Deck.
March Hare was banished: pay 300 LP, target March Hare itself, and **add it to your hand**.
March Hare's effect in hand: banish TB-11 from your GY to **Special Summon March Hare**.
**Link Summon Hearts Crypter** using both Chessy Cats + March Hare, to the Extra Monster Zone, so that it points to Red Ransom.

end.t: Hearts Crypter + Red Ransom + Maliss in Underground, and you still hold your other 4 cards. On either turn Hearts Crypter shuffles the banished TB-11 into your Deck to **banish 1 card on the field**, and that can't be negated. With Underground, their monsters can only attack your Maliss Links. You paid 2100 LP.

rules: Cynet Mining (add Dormouse), Gold Sarcophagus or Maliss in Underground (banish Dormouse from the Deck) start the same line. The last two keep your Normal Summon.
Put Red Ransom in a Main Monster Zone diagonally below the Extra Monster Zone when it returns in step 8. Hearts Crypter must point to a monster for its effect to be un-negatable.
Hearts Crypter needs a banished Maliss card each time. Here that is TB-11, then any Maliss monster you banish later.

combos.h: Line B — Kashtira first (going second)
combos.about: Fenrir and Unicorn only Summon themselves while you control no monsters, so they are always your first play. Wraitsoth finds Fenrir, Fenrir finds Unicorn for next turn, and you still have your Normal Summon and the whole Maliss line. In the Battle Phase Fenrir banishes one of their cards face-down.

steps.t: **Activate Pressured Planet Wraitsoth**: add Kashtira Fenrir from your Deck.
You control no monsters: **Special Summon Fenrir** from your hand.
Fenrir's effect: **add Kashtira Unicorn** from your Deck. Keep it for a turn when your field is empty again.
**Normal Summon Dormouse** and play Line A. Fenrir has no Extra Deck lock, so every Link is available.
Fenrir declares an attack: **banish 1 face-up card they control, face-down**. Then attack with everything.

end.t: Fenrir beside your Maliss Links, with Unicorn in hand. On their turn, the first monster effect they activate lets Fenrir banish another face-up card face-down.

rules: Line A step 6 replaces Wraitsoth with Maliss in Underground in the Field Zone. Wraitsoth has already searched, so nothing is lost.
Fenrir's search and its banish are each once per turn.
If they have a monster, a Bystial can also come first: it banishes a LIGHT or DARK monster from their GY as a Quick Effect.

combos.h: Line C — Accesscode Talker finish
combos.about: The going-second ending to Line A. Stop after Underground brings out Chessy Cat, and Link Red Ransom + Chessy Cat into Accesscode Talker. It gains 3000 ATK, then banishes Links from your GY to destroy a card each. They can't respond. Red Ransom is one of the Links you banish, so it Summons itself again and attacks too.

steps.t: Play Line A steps 1–6: you control **Red Ransom + Chessy Cat**, with Haggard Lizardose in your GY.
**Link Summon Accesscode Talker** using Red Ransom + Chessy Cat. Target Red Ransom: Accesscode gains 3000 ATK (5300).
Accesscode's effect: banish Lizardose (WATER) from your GY and **destroy 1 card** they control.
Use it again: banish Red Ransom (DARK) from your GY and **destroy a second card**.
Red Ransom was banished: pay 900 LP to **Special Summon it**, then banish March Hare from your Deck, which adds itself to your hand.
**Attack.** Accesscode has 5300 ATK and Red Ransom has 2900 (Dormouse gave Maliss monsters +600 this turn): 8200 damage on an empty field.

end.t: Two of their cards destroyed with no chance to respond, then 8200 damage from Accesscode Talker and Red Ransom. If they survive, the Set TB-11 and the March Hare in your hand restart the engine next turn.

rules: Accesscode can't banish two Links of the same Attribute in one turn. Lizardose is WATER and Red Ransom is DARK, so you get exactly two destroys.
Dormouse's +600 ATK applies to Maliss monsters only, not to Accesscode Talker.
You paid 1800 LP on this line. Check that their remaining cards can't punish that.

kashtira-maliss.arch: Maliss DARK Cyberse banish-loop Link combo with Bystials, a Kashtira empty-field package, Cynet Mining/Backup @Ignister Cyberse support and a large hand-trap suite.

runick-typhoon.pitch: A control deck of 37 Spells and 3 monsters. Each **Runick** Quick-Play Spell answers one of the opponent's cards and banishes cards from the top of their Deck. **Runick Fountain** lets you cast them on the opponent's turn and draws you back up. You win when they have no Deck left to draw from.

plan.first: Normal Summon **Inspector Boarder**, activate **Runick Fountain** and **Runick Allure**, and keep your Runick Spells in hand. On their turn you answer each play from your hand, and Fountain draws you up to 3 new cards.
plan.second: **Lightning Storm** or Harpie's Feather Duster first, while you control no face-up cards. Then Boarder and Fountain go down, and Forbidden Droplet, Flashing Fire and Destruction remove what is left.
plan.win: They lose when they have to draw and their Deck is empty. Every Runick Spell banishes 1 to 4 cards from it, and Allure adds 1 more for each Quick-Play. You rarely attack: every Runick Spell skips your next Battle Phase.

open.t: Adds any other Runick card: Fountain first, then whichever answer you need.
The engine. Runick Quick-Plays can be activated from your hand on their turn, and up to 3 used ones go back to the Deck to draw that many.
2000 ATK. Limits both players' monster effects to the number of Extra Deck monster types on the field, which is often zero.
Destroys a Special Summoned monster and banishes 2 cards from their Deck.

stops: **Losing Runick Fountain.** Without it you play at Spell Speed on your own turn only. Hugin can be banished to save it from destruction, and Geri or Multi-Universe bring it back.
**Your own Inspector Boarder.** It limits you too. Hugin's, Munin's and Geri's effects need a slot, and the Fusion you just Summoned provides exactly 1.
**Boards that are already built.** Runick Spells answer one card each. Going second, open with Lightning Storm, Feather Duster or Droplet, or Xyz Summon TY-PHON.

engines.t: 18 Quick-Play Spells. Each has two modes: its own effect plus a banish from the top of their Deck, **or** Special Summon a Runick Fusion from your Extra Deck. You can activate each name once per turn, and every one skips your next Battle Phase.

key.t: Add a Runick card from your Deck (not Tip). Banishes 1.
Destroy 1 Special Summoned monster. Banishes 2.
Negate 1 Effect Monster's effects this turn. Banishes 3.
Destroy 1 of their Spells/Traps. Banishes 4.
Your chosen monster survives the next destruction this turn (it can't attack). Banishes 3.
They draw 1 card, then you banish 4.
Banishes 1 card for each card they control.
When they add a card from Deck to hand: discard 1 random card from their hand. Banishes 2.

engines.t: The Fusions need no Fusion Spell: the second mode of any Runick Quick-Play Summons one to the Extra Monster Zone. They have 0 to 2000 ATK and exist to fetch and protect your Spells.

key.t: Field Spell. Lets you activate Runick Quick-Plays from hand on their turn. Once per turn: put up to 3 from your GY on the bottom of the Deck and draw that many.
Continuous Spell. Banishes their top card every time any Quick-Play Spell is activated, including Droplet, Mystical Space Typhoon and Vision.
Summoned: discard 1 to add Runick Fountain. If another card of yours would be destroyed by an effect, banish Hugin instead.
Summoned: discard 1 to add Runick Allure. Banish it to negate an effect that targets your Runick cards or Set cards.
Summoned: return Fountain or Allure from your GY to your hand. Can't be destroyed by card effects.
Quick Effect: banish itself and 1 of their monsters until the End Phase.

engines.t: **Inspector Boarder** ×3 limits monster effects. **Dimensional Fissure** ×2 banishes every monster that would go to the GY. **Radiant Typhoon Vision** ×3 draws 2 (then discard a Quick-Play Spell) or adds Mystical Space Typhoon. Pot of Desires ×2 and Pot of Duality dig for Fountain.

**Lightning Storm** and **Harpie's Feather Duster** clear a field. **Forbidden Droplet** ×2 negates monsters. **TY-PHON** ×3 is an Xyz Monster made from just 1 monster after they Summon twice from the Extra Deck. **S:P Little Knight** ×2 banishes a card.

facts.t: **Every Runick Quick-Play skips your next Battle Phase**, whichever mode you use. That is why the deck wins by emptying their Deck and why Evenly Matched is not run.

**One of each name per turn.** You can activate only 1 Runick Tip per turn, 1 Flashing Fire, and so on. That counts both players' turns separately, so each name works once on your turn and once on theirs.
**Inspector Boarder can't be Summoned if you control a monster.** Summon it before any Runick Fusion. With one Fusion on the field, each player gets 1 monster effect per turn.
**Lightning Storm needs you to control no face-up cards.** Activate it before Fountain, Allure, Dimensional Fissure or Boarder.

**Mystical Space Typhoon, Forbidden Droplet and Vision are Quick-Plays but not Runick cards.** They trigger Allure, but Fountain can't recycle them or let you activate them from hand on their turn. Set them.
**Pot of Duality stops you Special Summoning that turn**, so don't use a Runick Spell's Summon mode after it. Pot of Desires banishes 10 of your own cards face-down.
**Radiant Typhoon Vision** draws 2 and then makes you discard a Quick-Play Spell or Radiant Typhoon card. If you have neither, you discard your whole hand.

str: Answers come from the hand on the opponent's turn, so there is little for them to remove first.
Fountain draws up to 3 cards a turn, so you don't run out.
Inspector Boarder and Dimensional Fissure shut down many decks by themselves.
Real going-second cards: Lightning Storm, Feather Duster, Droplet ×2, TY-PHON ×3.
weak: Almost everything depends on Runick Fountain staying on the field.
No Battle Phase most turns, so games are long and a stalled opponent can recover.
Inspector Boarder restricts your own Runick Fusions.
Each Runick Spell handles one card: a full board going second needs a breaker.

combos.h: Plan A — Boarder, Fountain and Allure (going first)
combos.about: Turn one is set-up. Inspector Boarder goes down first because it needs an empty field. Tip finds Fountain. A second Runick Spell is used in Summon mode for Munin, who finds Allure, and Fountain turns the used Tip into a new card. You keep your answers in hand for their turn.

steps.t: **Normal Summon Inspector Boarder** while you control no monsters.
Activate Runick Tip, first effect: **add Runick Fountain** and banish the top card of their Deck.
**Activate Runick Fountain** in your Field Zone.
Activate Runick Slumber, second effect: **Special Summon Munin** to the Extra Monster Zone.
You activated a Runick Quick-Play, so Fountain triggers: put Tip from your GY on the bottom of your Deck and **draw 1**.
Munin was Summoned: discard the card you need least and **add Runick Allure**. Activate it.

end.t: Boarder + Munin + Fountain + Allure, with Flashing Fire and Freezing Curses in hand. On their turn: Flashing Fire destroys a Special Summoned monster, Freezing Curses negates a monster, Allure banishes 1 extra card each time, and Fountain puts the used Spells back to draw up to 3.

rules: No Tip? Use any Runick Spell's Summon mode for **Hugin** instead: discard 1 and it adds Fountain.
With Boarder and Munin (a Fusion) on the field, each player gets 1 monster effect per turn. Munin's search uses yours.
If they target Fountain or Allure, banish Munin to negate that effect and destroy the card.

combos.h: Their turn — Which Runick Spell answers what
combos.about: With Runick Fountain on the field you activate these from your hand during the opponent's turn. Use each one on the card it is best against, then let Fountain return up to 3 of them to your Deck and draw that many. Each name can be activated once per turn.

rows.when: They Special Summon a key monster
rows.t: Destroy it. Banishes the top 2 cards of their Deck.

rows.when: A monster on the field activates an effect
rows.t: Chain it to negate that monster's effects for the turn. Banishes 3.

rows.when: They Set or activate a Spell/Trap that stays on the field
rows.t: Destroy it. Banishes 4.

rows.when: They try to destroy Boarder or attack over it
rows.t: Target your own monster: the next time it would be destroyed this turn, it isn't. Banishes 3.
Discards 1 random card from their hand. Banishes 2.
Golden Droplet banishes 4 (they draw 1). Smiting Storm banishes 1 per card they control.

rules: Runick Allure banishes 1 more card every time a Quick-Play Spell is activated.
Fountain's recycle is once per turn. It only targets Runick Quick-Plays already in your GY, so trigger it with your second or third Spell.
The second mode (Summon a Fusion) is still there on their turn: Hugin to protect Fountain, or Sleipnir to banish an attacker.

combos.h: Plan B — Breaking a board (going second)
combos.about: Going second you clear the field before you set up. Lightning Storm only works while you control no face-up cards, so it comes first. Then Boarder and Fountain go down, and each Quick-Play removes one more card while thinning their Deck.

steps.t: You control no face-up cards: **activate Lightning Storm**. Destroy all their Attack Position monsters, or all their Spells and Traps.
**Normal Summon Inspector Boarder** while you control no monsters.
**Activate Runick Fountain.**
Activate Runick Destruction: **destroy 1 Spell/Trap** they control and banish the top 4 cards of their Deck.
Activate Forbidden Droplet: send 1 other card from your hand or field to the GY to halve the ATK of 1 of their monsters and **negate its effects**.
Activate Runick Flashing Fire: **destroy 1 Special Summoned monster** and banish 2. Fountain returns Destruction to your Deck and you draw 1.

end.t: Inspector Boarder + Runick Fountain against a broken board, with their Deck 6 cards thinner. Boarder now limits what they can rebuild with, and you skip your next Battle Phase.

rules: Harpie's Feather Duster does the Spell/Trap half of Lightning Storm with no condition.
Forbidden Droplet can't be responded to by the card types you sent as its cost.
Destruction, Droplet and Flashing Fire are all Quick-Plays: with Allure out, each banishes 1 more card.

combos.h: Plan C — TY-PHON from one monster
combos.about: Super Starslayer TY-PHON normally needs two Level 12 monsters. It has a shortcut: during the turn your opponent Special Summoned 2 or more monsters from the Extra Deck, or the turn after, you can Xyz Summon it using only your highest-ATK monster. It answers boards that single Runick Spells can't.

steps.t: They Special Summon 2 or more monsters from the Extra Deck. You control Inspector Boarder or Freki (2000 ATK).
On your turn, **Xyz Summon TY-PHON** using only your highest-ATK monster. You can't Normal or Special Summon for the rest of the turn.
Detach the material: **return 1 monster on the field to the hand**. An Extra Deck monster goes back to the Extra Deck.

end.t: TY-PHON (2900 ATK) with their best monster gone. While TY-PHON is on the field, neither player can activate the effects of monsters with 3000 or more ATK.

rules: Using Inspector Boarder as the material gives up its lock. Use Freki when you have it.
The deck runs 3 TY-PHON because the Summon uses up the monster each time.
TY-PHON is an Xyz Monster, so with a Boarder still on the field it adds 1 monster-effect slot for each player.

runick-typhoon.arch: Runick Quick-Play mill/control with Inspector Boarder and Dimensional Fissure floodgates, a going-second breaker package (Lightning Storm, Harpie's Feather Duster, Forbidden Droplet ×2, Mystical Space Typhoon ×2), and TY-PHON ×3.

ryu-ge-mitsurugi.pitch: Two Ritual engines in one deck. The **Mitsurugi** Reptiles wipe the opponent's monsters and tax their effects. The **Ryu-Ge** Level 10s fill your field in one play, then **Sosei Ryu-Ge Mistva** trades them for three **Realm** Spells that give it three different Quick Effects.

plan.first: Mitsurugi first: Ritual Summon **Murakumo** and **Futsu** and Set Great Purification. Then **Ryu-Ge War Zone** Summons three Level 10s, and **Mistva** arrives with all three Realms.
plan.second: Murakumo destroys every monster they control when it is Summoned, and Anva destroys 1 more card. Then set up the Realms so they can't rebuild.
plan.win: 3000+ ATK monsters that negate, bounce and shrink on the opponent's turn. Two Level 10s can also overlay into **Gustav Max** for 2000 damage on a turn without War Zone.

open.t: Discard 1 card to add Anva **and** Mistva. Mistva then finds War Zone, so this is the whole Ryu-Ge line.
Adds any Ryu-Ge monster, usually Mistva, and can put it straight into your face-up Extra Deck.
Adds any Mitsurugi monster. Tribute a Reptile on activation to also Summon one from hand or GY.
Adds Mitsurugi Mirror and Murakumo (or Futsu) together.

stops: **The order.** War Zone only lets you Special Summon Dragons, Dinosaurs, Sea Serpents and Wyrms for the rest of the turn. Mitsurugi monsters are Reptiles, so play them **before** War Zone.
**Ash Blossom on War Zone.** Put an Anva from your hand in a Pendulum Zone first. Its Pendulum Effect negates a card they chain to your Ryu-Ge Spell.
**Drawing the wrong Level 10.** War Zone needs Kaiva, Emva **and** Hakva in the Deck, and there is 1 of each. Kaiva can shuffle itself back from your hand; the other two can't.

engines.t: Level 10 monsters of four different Types. Ryu-Ge War Zone takes three from the Deck and then Summons three at once, but only while Mistva is face-up in your Extra Deck.

key.t: Pendulum Ritual Monster, 3500 ATK. In a Pendulum Zone: add a Ryu-Ge card (War Zone), then it destroys itself and goes to the Extra Deck face-up. From there it Summons itself when a monster is destroyed.
On activation: take a Dinosaur, a Sea Serpent and a Wyrm from your Deck (1 to hand, 1 banished, 1 to GY). Then, with Mistva face-up in the Extra Deck, Summon 3 Ryu-Ge from Deck, GY and banishment.
Tribute another Ryu-Ge to Summon it from hand. Special Summoned: destroy 1 card. Destroyed: place a Realm. In a Pendulum Zone it protects your Ryu-Ge Spells.
Discard 1: add up to 2 Dragons with 3000+ ATK and 2500 or less DEF. Anva and Mistva both qualify.
Adds a Ryu-Ge monster, then can move a Ryu-Ge Pendulum from your hand to the face-up Extra Deck.
Dinosaur. Quick Effect: Summons itself from hand if 2+ cards were destroyed this turn.
Sea Serpent. With Sea Spires, banishes their whole hand and makes them draw that many.
Wyrm. With Wyrm Winds, adds any Ryu-Ge card from Deck, GY or banishment.

engines.t: Continuous Spells. Each gives its Quick Effect to every Ryu-Ge **Pendulum** Monster you control (Mistva and Anva get all three) and to the Level 10 of the matching Type. Using an effect costs you one Realm: it goes to the bottom of your Deck.

key.t: Ryu-Ge monsters gain 300 ATK. **Negate** the activation of an effect from a monster on the field with less ATK than the monster using this.
On their turn, monsters sent from the field to the GY are banished instead. Once per opponent's turn: make 1 face-up monster's **ATK 0**.
Your Ryu-Ge monsters can't be destroyed by battle. Once per opponent's turn: **return 1 card** on the field to the hand.

engines.t: DARK Reptile Rituals. The Level 4 Mikoto monsters search when they are **Tributed**, so paying for a Ritual Summon refills your hand. All of it must happen before War Zone.

key.t: Level 8 Ritual. Special Summoned: destroy all their monsters. Quick Effect: when they activate anything, they discard 1 card or it is negated.
Level 8 Ritual, 3400 DEF. When they Special Summon, it revives a Reptile from your GY.
Summoned or Tributed: adds a Mitsurugi monster.
Summoned or Tributed: adds a Mitsurugi Spell/Trap.
Summoned or Tributed: returns a Mitsurugi card from your GY or banishment.
Ritual Spell. Summons a Reptile Ritual from hand or GY by Tributing Reptiles from hand or field.
Ritual Summons from hand by Tributing from the **Deck**, or from the Deck by Tributing from hand or field.
Trap. Tribute a Level 5+ Reptile to negate and destroy. Murakumo or Futsu then searches and returns.

engines.t: **Ringowurm** is the only Tuner: with a Level 10 it makes **Snake-Eyes Vengeance Dragon** or **Crimson Dragon**, with a Mitsurugi Level 8 it makes Chengying, Chaos Angel or Ruddy Rose Dragon. Two Level 10s make **Gustav Max** or Number 35. Ash Blossom ×3, Infinite Impermanence ×2, Bystial Magnamhut, Droll and Nibiru are the hand traps.
cards: Ringowurm, the Dragon Guarding the Hundred Apples

facts.t: **War Zone's lock stops Reptiles.** After it resolves you can't Ritual Summon or revive any Mitsurugi monster that turn. It also blocks the Xyz and Link Monsters; the Dragon and Wyrm Synchros are fine.

**Mistva can only be Summoned from the face-up Extra Deck**, by its own effect, once per turn, and it needs a Level 10 Ryu-Ge on your field to Tribute. A monster on the field must be destroyed first: Anva's Summon effect does that.
**War Zone needs one Dinosaur, one Sea Serpent and one Wyrm in your Deck.** Kaiva, Emva and Hakva are the only ones. If Emva or Hakva is in your hand, GY or banishment, War Zone can't be activated.
**Pre-Preparation of Rites only works with Mitsurugi Mirror**, because Mirror is the Ritual Spell that names Murakumo and Futsu.
**Crimson Dragon can become Cosmic Blazar Dragon.** Its Quick Effect targets a Level 12 Synchro (Vengeance Dragon), returns itself, and Summons a Level 12 Dragon Synchro as a Synchro Summon.
**Ringowurm only Summons itself from hand if a non-Effect Monster is on the field**, which depends on your opponent. Plan to Normal Summon it.
cards: Ringowurm, the Dragon Guarding the Hundred Apples

str: Murakumo's wipe plus Anva's destroy clears boards going second.
Three Realms mean three different Quick Effects on their turn.
Melody, Rising, Prayers and Pre-Preparation are all one-card starts.
Every monster that matters has 3000 or more ATK.
weak: War Zone locks out the Mitsurugi half, the Xyz Monsters and the Links.
One copy each of War Zone, Kaiva, Emva and Hakva: a bad draw breaks the Ryu-Ge line.
Ringowurm is the only Tuner.
Many pieces are Level 8 or 10 and do nothing alone in your hand.

combos.h: Line A — Mitsurugi before War Zone
combos.about: The Ritual half, played first because War Zone would lock it out. Pre-Preparation finds Mirror and Murakumo, and Prayers finds a Level 4 to pay for it. Murakumo destroys every monster they control. Saji, Tributed, finds Mitsurugi Ritual, which Tributes Murakumo to bring Futsu from the Deck, and Murakumo comes straight back.

steps.t: Activate Pre-Preparation of Rites: **add Mitsurugi Mirror and Murakumo** from your Deck.
Activate Mitsurugi Prayers without Tributing: **add Aramasa**.
**Normal Summon Aramasa.** It adds Saji from your Deck.
Activate Mirror: **Ritual Summon Murakumo** from your hand by Tributing Aramasa (field) + Saji (hand), Level 4 + 4.
Murakumo was Special Summoned: **destroy all monsters they control**. Saji was Tributed: add Mitsurugi Ritual.
Activate Mitsurugi Ritual, first effect: **Ritual Summon Futsu from your Deck** by Tributing Murakumo (Level 8).
Murakumo was Tributed: **add Great Purification**, then Murakumo Special Summons itself. Set Great Purification.

end.t: Murakumo + Futsu with Great Purification Set. When they activate something, Murakumo makes them discard 1 card or it is negated. When they Special Summon, Futsu revives Aramasa or Saji, which searches. Great Purification Tributes Futsu to negate and destroy, and Futsu returns.

rules: Do this before Ryu-Ge War Zone, never after.
Aramasa already searched when it was Normal Summoned, so it doesn't search again when Tributed. Each Mikoto effect is once per turn.
Murakumo's wipe is once per turn: it doesn't destroy again when it returns.

combos.h: Line B — Melody into Mistva and three Realms
combos.about: The Ryu-Ge half from one Spell. Melody finds Mistva and Anva. Mistva, placed in a Pendulum Zone, finds War Zone and puts itself in the Extra Deck face-up. War Zone then Summons three Level 10s, Anva destroys one of them, and that destruction lets Mistva Summon itself and swap your cards for Realms.

steps.t: Activate Melody: discard 1 card (here Nibiru) and **add Anva and Mistva** from your Deck.
Place Mistva in a Pendulum Zone. Its effect **adds Ryu-Ge War Zone**, then Mistva destroys itself and goes to your Extra Deck face-up.
**Activate War Zone.** Take Kaiva, Emva and Hakva from your Deck: Kaiva to your hand, Hakva banished, Emva to the GY.
War Zone's effect: **Special Summon 3 Ryu-Ge**: a second Anva from your Deck, Emva from the GY and Hakva from banishment.
Anva was Special Summoned: target Emva and **destroy it**.
A monster was destroyed: Tribute Hakva to **Special Summon Mistva** from your Extra Deck (a Ritual Summon).
Mistva's effect: destroy War Zone and Anva, then **place Wyrm Winds and Sea Spires** from your Deck.
Anva was destroyed: **place Dino Domains** from your Deck.
2 or more cards were destroyed this turn: **Special Summon Kaiva** from your hand.

end.t: Mistva (3800 ATK) + Kaiva (3300) + all three Realms, with an Anva still in hand. On their turn Mistva can negate a monster effect, return a card to the hand and make a monster's ATK 0. Each use puts one Realm on the bottom of your Deck. Kaiva can use the negate too.

rules: Ryu-Ge Rising starts this too: add Mistva, then place it in a Pendulum Zone yourself (step 2).
Before step 3, put the Anva from your hand in your other Pendulum Zone. If they chain Ash Blossom to War Zone, Anva negates it.
After War Zone you can only Special Summon Dragons, Dinosaurs, Sea Serpents and Wyrms this turn.

combos.h: Line C — Ringowurm adds a Level 12
combos.about: Ringowurm is a Level 2 Tuner. Kaiva is the one monster from Line B that the Realms don't need, so Kaiva + Ringowurm becomes Snake-Eyes Vengeance Dragon, a Level 12 Dragon that War Zone's lock allows. Ringowurm then leaves a Tuner Token behind for next turn.
hand: Ringowurm, the Dragon Guarding the Hundred Apples
combos.ns: Ringowurm, the Dragon Guarding the Hundred Apples

steps.t: After Line B, **Normal Summon Ringowurm** (Level 2 Tuner).
cards: Ringowurm, the Dragon Guarding the Hundred Apples

steps.t: **Synchro Summon Snake-Eyes Vengeance Dragon** (Level 12) using Ringowurm + Kaiva (Level 10).
cards: Ringowurm, the Dragon Guarding the Hundred Apples

steps.t: You Synchro Summoned this turn: banish Ringowurm from your GY to **Special Summon a Hundred Apples Token** (Level 2, can be used as a Tuner).
cards: Ringowurm, the Dragon Guarding the Hundred Apples

end.t: Mistva with three Realms + Snake-Eyes Vengeance Dragon + a Tuner Token. Vengeance Dragon adds a fourth Quick Effect: it moves a monster to the Spell & Trap Zone as a Continuous Spell.
cards: Ringowurm, the Dragon Guarding the Hundred Apples

rules: Next turn the Token + a Level 10 makes **Crimson Dragon**. Target Vengeance Dragon with its Quick Effect to swap it for **Cosmic Blazar Dragon**, which negates an activation, a Summon or an attack.
Don't use Mistva as Synchro Material while the Realms are out. Without a Ryu-Ge Pendulum or matching Level 10, nobody can use them.
Without War Zone this turn, Ringowurm + Murakumo or Futsu (Level 8) makes Chengying, Chaos Angel or Ruddy Rose Dragon instead.

ryu-ge-mitsurugi.arch: Ryu-Ge Level 10 Pendulum/Realm control fused with the Mitsurugi DARK Reptile Ritual engine, Ringowurm Synchro access and a Rank 10/11/12 Xyz toolbox.

scareclaw-kashtira.pitch: An attack deck built around Defense Position. **Scareclaw Tri-Heart** turns every face-up monster on the field to Defense Position and ignores the effects of Defense Position monsters. Your small Scareclaws then give it more ATK, extra attacks and piercing damage. The **Kashtira** monsters add free Level 7s that banish cards face-down.

plan.first: One Reichheart becomes **Tri-Heart** with two Scareclaws and the Field Spell Reichphobia. If you also open Fenrir, Summon it first. Their monsters arrive in Defense Position and can't affect Tri-Heart.
plan.second: Super Polymerization and Infinite Impermanence open the way. Build the same board, destroy 1 card with Reichphobia, then Tri-Heart attacks up to three times with piercing damage.
plan.win: Tri-Heart at 3600 to 3900 ATK attacking once for each different Scareclaw you control in Defense Position, with Belone making every attack pierce.

open.t: The one-card combo. Normal Summon it to add Scareclaw Arrival, then Link it into Light-Heart.
Field Spell. Adds Reichheart (or any Scareclaw monster or Visas Starfrost) when activated.
Special Summons itself while you control no monsters, and adds another Kashtira. Play it before anything else.
Going second: fuses away two of their monsters with no response.

stops: **The first Scareclaw.** Acro, Belone, Astra and Reichheart only Summon themselves next to, or in the column of, a Scareclaw you already control. If Reichheart or Light-Heart is stopped, the rest stay in your hand.
**Tri-Heart's lock.** After its revive effect you can only Special Summon Scareclaw monsters that turn. Use Super Polymerization, S:P Little Knight or Visas plays before it.
**Fenrir and Unicorn need an empty field.** Drawn late, they need Kashtira Birth, which lets you Normal Summon Level 7s without Tributing.

engines.t: Reichheart starts everything. Light-Heart finds the Field Spell, the Level 3 Beasts Summon themselves from hand, and three Effect Monsters become Tri-Heart. Each Level 3 gives a bonus to your Scareclaw in the **Extra Monster Zone**.

key.t: Level 4. Summoned: add a Scareclaw Spell/Trap. Can Summon itself from hand next to a Scareclaw.
Link-1 made from 1 Scareclaw in a Main Monster Zone. Link Summoned to the Extra Monster Zone: add Reichphobia.
Field Spell. Adds a Scareclaw monster. Their monsters lose 100 ATK/DEF per Defense Position monster. With 3+ in Defense: destroy 1 of their cards, once per turn.
Link-3, 3000 ATK. All face-up monsters become Defense Position. Unaffected by activated effects of Defense Position monsters. Revives a Level 3 Scareclaw and adds a Scareclaw monster.
Your Extra Monster Zone Scareclaw gains 300 ATK for each Defense Position monster you control.
It can attack once for each Defense Position Scareclaw you control with a different name.
It deals piercing damage when it attacks a Defense Position monster.
Spell. Special Summons a Scareclaw monster or Visas Starfrost from your GY in Defense Position.

engines.t: Level 7 Psychics that need no Normal Summon. They answer the opponent's monster effects by banishing face-down, which very few decks can undo.

key.t: Adds a Kashtira monster. When it attacks, or when they activate a monster effect: banish 1 of their face-up cards face-down.
Adds Kashtira Birth. When it attacks, or when they activate a monster effect: banish 1 monster from their Extra Deck face-down.
Counts as both names. Quick Effect: Summons itself from hand in either Main Phase. Attacks from Defense Position using its 2600 DEF, and negates the monster it battles.
Continuous Spell. Normal Summon Level 7s without Tributing, and Special Summon a banished or GY Kashtira once per turn.
Rank 7 Xyz from two Level 7s. Each time their card is banished face-down, you lock one of their unused zones.

engines.t: **Visas Starfrost** Summons itself by destroying one of your own monsters of a different Type and Attribute. With a 1500 ATK / 2100 DEF monster (Reichheart or Visas Samsara) it makes **Vicious Astraloud**, which destroys a monster when Summoned. S:P Little Knight, Accesscode Talker, Chaos Angel, I:P Masquerena and TY-PHON cover the rest.
Ash Blossom ×3, Infinite Impermanence ×3, Ghost Ogre ×3, Nibiru ×2, Effect Veiler, Droll & Lock Bird and Mulcharmy Fuwalos. **Super Polymerization** ×3 with four Fusion targets.

facts.t: **Scareclaw monsters Summon themselves only to a Main Monster Zone next to a Scareclaw you control, or in its column.** A Scareclaw Link in the Extra Monster Zone opens the zone directly below it.
**Light-Heart** can only use a monster in your Main Monster Zone as material, and it searches only when Link Summoned into the **Extra Monster Zone**.
**Acro, Astra and Belone only help a Scareclaw in the Extra Monster Zone.** Keep Tri-Heart there.

**Visas Starfrost** needs a target with a different Type **and** Attribute (it is a LIGHT Warrior). Reichheart (Warrior) and Visas Samsara (LIGHT) don't qualify. The Level 3 Beasts and the Kashtiras do.
**Vicious Astraloud is not a Super Polymerization target.** You Summon it by banishing Visas Starfrost and a 1500 ATK / 2100 DEF monster from your field or GY.
**Reichphobia's destroy effect** counts Defense Position monsters on both sides of the field, and Tri-Heart puts their monsters in Defense too.

str: Reichheart, Reichphobia and Reinforcement of the Army are all one-card combos into Tri-Heart.
Tri-Heart ignores the effects of almost every monster, because it puts them in Defense Position.
Kashtira is a second opening that doesn't use the Normal Summon.
17 hand traps and breakers, including 3 Super Polymerization.
weak: If the first Scareclaw is stopped, the rest of the hand can't Summon itself.
Tri-Heart's revive effect locks you to Scareclaws for the turn.
Fenrir and Unicorn are weak draws once you already control a monster.
Light-Heart's revival from the GY works once per Duel.

combos.h: Line A — Reichheart into Tri-Heart
combos.about: A full board from one card. Reichheart finds the Spell Arrival and becomes Light-Heart, which finds the Field Spell. Reichphobia adds Acro, Arrival brings Reichheart back, and the three monsters Link into Tri-Heart. Tri-Heart then revives Acro and adds Astra.

steps.t: **Normal Summon Reichheart.** It adds Scareclaw Arrival from your Deck.
**Link Summon Light-Heart** to the Extra Monster Zone using Reichheart. It adds Primitive Planet Reichphobia.
**Activate Reichphobia**: add Scareclaw Acro from your Deck.
Activate Arrival: **Special Summon Reichheart** from your GY in Defense Position.
**Special Summon Acro** from your hand to the zone below Light-Heart or next to Reichheart.
**Link Summon Tri-Heart** to the Extra Monster Zone using Light-Heart + Reichheart + Acro. Every face-up monster becomes Defense Position.
Tri-Heart's effect: **Special Summon Acro** from your GY and add Scareclaw Astra. You can only Special Summon Scareclaws for the rest of the turn.
**Special Summon Astra** from your hand next to Acro.

end.t: Tri-Heart (3600 ATK) + Acro + Astra + Reichphobia, and you still hold your other 4 cards. Anything they Summon face-up goes to Defense Position, and Tri-Heart ignores those monsters' activated effects. Their monsters lose 100 ATK/DEF per Defense Position monster.

rules: Reichphobia (adds Reichheart) and Reinforcement of the Army start the same line.
Reichheart's search is once per turn, so the copy Arrival brings back doesn't search again.
Make any non-Scareclaw Extra Deck monster before step 7.

combos.h: Line B — Fenrir first
combos.about: Kashtira Fenrir Summons itself only while you control no monsters, so it comes before the Scareclaws. It adds Scareclaw Kashtira, a monster you keep in hand and Summon as a Quick Effect on their turn. Then Line A goes ahead as normal. Fenrir doesn't restrict it.

steps.t: You control no monsters: **Special Summon Kashtira Fenrir** from your hand.
Fenrir's effect: **add Scareclaw Kashtira** from your Deck.
Play Line A with Reichheart, ending on **Tri-Heart** + Acro + Astra. Fenrir moves to Defense Position but keeps its effects.
Their Main Phase: **Special Summon Scareclaw Kashtira** from your hand (Quick Effect), then banish 1 Scareclaw card from your GY.
When they activate a monster effect, Fenrir **banishes 1 face-up card they control, face-down**.

end.t: Tri-Heart + Fenrir + Acro + Astra, with Scareclaw Kashtira arriving on their turn. Any monster that battles your Scareclaw or Kashtira monsters has its effects negated for the turn.

rules: Don't add Kashtira Unicorn in step 2 unless you have Kashtira Birth. It can't Summon itself while Fenrir is on your field.
Fenrir counts as a Defense Position monster for Acro's ATK boost and Reichphobia.
Two Level 7s can overlay into Kashtira Shangri-Ira, but do it before Tri-Heart's lock.

combos.h: Line C — Tri-Heart attack (going second)
combos.about: The same board, used to win the turn you build it. With three different Scareclaws in Defense Position, Tri-Heart attacks three times. Acro gives it 300 ATK for each of your Defense Position monsters, and Belone makes its attacks pierce. Tri-Heart has already turned their monsters to Defense Position, so they have no ATK to hit back with.

steps.t: Play Line A: **Tri-Heart** in the Extra Monster Zone with Acro and Astra in Defense Position.
**Special Summon Belone** from your hand next to a Scareclaw. It is a Scareclaw, so Tri-Heart's lock allows it.
3 or more Defense Position monsters are on the field: Reichphobia **destroys 1 card they control**.
**Attack with Tri-Heart**: 3000 + 900 from Acro = 3900 ATK, up to 3 attacks (Acro, Astra and Belone are three names).
Each attack into a Defense Position monster **pierces** because of Belone. When their monsters run out, it attacks directly.

end.t: Three attacks at 3900 ATK. Their monsters are in Defense Position and have lost 100 DEF for every Defense Position monster on the field, so most of each attack goes through as damage.

rules: Use Super Polymerization and Infinite Impermanence before you start. A negated Reichheart ends the turn.
Astra counts different **names**: two Acros are still one attack.
Reichphobia's destroy is once per turn.

combos.h: Going second — Super Polymerization
combos.about: **Super Polymerization** is a Quick-Play Spell: discard 1 card, then Fusion Summon using monsters from **either** field. Neither player can respond to it. Two of their best monsters (or one of theirs and one of yours) become one Fusion Monster on your side. The materials are sent to the GY without being targeted or destroyed, so their protection doesn't help. Pick the Fusion by what the two monsters share:

rows.t: Gains the ATK of one of their Special Summoned monsters this turn, and can copy the name and effects of a Level 5+ monster they control. **Your own:** Reichheart, Light-Heart and Tri-Heart are all DARK.

Any 2 monsters with different names. Garura doubles the battle damage it deals and draws you 1 card when it goes to the GY. **Your own pair:** two different Level 3 Scareclaws (EARTH Beasts), or Fenrir + Scareclaw Kashtira (EARTH Psychics).
Your opponent can't target Mudragon, or any monster sharing its Attribute, with card effects. **Your own pair:** a Level 3 Scareclaw (Beast) + Fenrir (Psychic), both EARTH.
Gains 1000 ATK when it battles a monster with 2200+ ATK, and can Fusion Summon again after a monster is destroyed by battle. **Your own pair:** Fenrir (EARTH) + Unicorn (WIND), both Psychic.

rules: You choose the Fusion when Super Polymerization resolves, so check each monster's Type and Attribute before you activate it.
Use it before Tri-Heart's revive effect: that lock stops non-Scareclaw Special Summons, Fusions included.
You can also Set it and activate it on your opponent's turn, in the middle of their combo.

scareclaw-kashtira.arch: Defense-Position beatdown/OTK (Scareclaw) with a Kashtira banish-disruption package and Visas Starfrost glue, plus a Super Polymerization removal toolbox.

earthbound-resonator.pitch: A Synchro deck built on **Red Dragon Archfiend**. Small Fiend Tuners called Resonators search each other and climb into Level 8 and 9 DARK Dragon Synchros. **Earthbound Immortal Red Nova** turns one of them into Red Nova Dragon on either turn, and a small **Horus** engine gives the deck a second way to play.

plan.first: One Soul Resonator becomes **The Crimson King** and **Hot Red Dragon Archfiend Abyss**, with Crimson Gaia face-up. Abyss negates a card, and the King answers a monster effect by Summoning Red Dragon Archfiend at 6000 ATK.
plan.second: The same line, but let **Scarred Dragon Archfiend** use its effect: it Summons Red Dragon Archfiend and destroys all their Attack Position monsters. Super Polymerization goes first, on a turn before the Resonator locks.
plan.win: Three Dragons with 3000+ ATK attack for game after the wipe. In longer games Red Nova Dragon (5000+ ATK, can't be destroyed by their effects) and the Horus monsters take over.

open.t: The starter. Normal Summon it to add Bone Archfiend, and the whole line follows.
Adds Soul Resonator or any other Resonator.
Discard it to add Soul Resonator (a Level 3 Fiend Tuner). It can also Summon itself while a Field Spell is out.
Continuous Spell. Each turn it adds Red Dragon Archfiend or a card that mentions it, which includes Soul, Vision and Darkness Resonator.
The Horus opening. Its cost sends a second card to the GY: make it a Vision Resonator.

stops: **The locks.** Soul Resonator, Bone Archfiend, Power Vice and Crimson Resonator each restrict your Extra Deck to DARK (Dragon) Synchros for the turn. S:P Little Knight, TY-PHON, Chengying and the Fusions can't be Summoned on a Resonator turn.
**Red Dragon Archfiend's End Phase.** It destroys your other monsters that didn't attack. Going first, don't Summon it on your own turn: use Scarred or The Crimson King as your Level 8.
**Ash Blossom on Soul Resonator.** Resonator Call, Stone Sweeper and Crimson Gaia each find another way in, and the Horus engine doesn't depend on it at all.

engines.t: Level 2 and 3 Fiend Tuners plus the non-Tuners they are added to. Level 3 + Level 5 is the sum you are looking for: it makes a Level 8.

key.t: Level 3 Tuner. Summoned: add a Level 4 or lower Fiend (Bone Archfiend). In the GY it can be banished to save your cards from destruction.
Level 4. Send 1 other card from hand or field to Summon it from hand or GY. Then send a Fiend Tuner from your Deck to the GY to make a monster's Level 1 higher or lower.
Level 2 Tuner. Summons itself if a Level 5+ DARK monster is on the field. Sent to the GY: add a Spell/Trap that mentions Red Dragon Archfiend (Crimson Gaia).
Level 5 Dragon. Summons itself if all your monsters are DARK Synchros, then adds a Resonator.
Level 3 Tuner. Reveal Red Dragon Archfiend in your Extra Deck to Summon it. Can change your Tuners' Levels to 1.
Level 2 Tuner. Summons itself on an empty field. Next to exactly 1 DARK Dragon Synchro it Summons 2 Resonators from hand or Deck.
Level 5. Discard to add a Level 3 or lower Fiend Tuner.
Adds a Red Dragon Archfiend card each turn, and revives Red Dragon Archfiend from the GY when a monster is destroyed.

engines.t: DARK Dragon Synchros. Several of them Summon the original Red Dragon Archfiend from the Extra Deck, and there is only 1 copy, so only one of those effects pays off per game.

key.t: Level 8. Synchro Summoned: add a card that mentions Red Dragon Archfiend. When they activate a monster effect: banish it to Summon Red Dragon Archfiend with doubled ATK.
Level 8. Its name is Red Dragon Archfiend on the field and in the GY. Sent to the GY: Summon Red Dragon Archfiend. If it was Synchro Material, also destroy all their Attack Position monsters.
Level 9. Quick Effect: negate the effects of 1 face-up card they control until the end of the turn.
Level 8. After it attacks a Defense Position monster, destroy all their Defense Position monsters. In your End Phase it destroys your other monsters that didn't attack.
Main Deck Level 12. Quick Effect from hand or GY: banish it and send Red Dragon Archfiend from your field to the GY to Summon Red Nova Dragon.
Level 12. Gains 500 ATK per Tuner in your GY, can't be destroyed by their card effects, and can banish itself to negate an attack.
Level 12 made from 3 Tuners + a Synchro. Banishes itself and every card they control when they attack or activate a monster effect.
Level 10. Summons a banished LIGHT or DARK monster, and can negate a monster effect by shuffling a banished card back.

engines.t: **Imsety** ×3 and **Hapi** Summon themselves from the GY while you control **King's Sarcophagus** ×2. They need no Normal Summon and no Extra Deck, so no Resonator lock touches them. Their costs put Vision Resonator and Bone Archfiend into the GY, where both are useful.

**Super Polymerization** ×3 with Garura, Mudragon and Flame Wingman. **Terraforming** finds **Chicken Game**, which lets Stone Sweeper Summon itself and draws a card for 1000 LP. Ash Blossom ×3, Infinite Impermanence ×2, Ghost Ogre ×2, Effect Veiler, Droll and Nibiru are the hand traps.

facts.t: **There is 1 Red Dragon Archfiend in the Extra Deck.** The Crimson King, Scarred Dragon Archfiend and Crimson Gaia all want it. Once it is in the GY, Crimson Gaia can revive it.
**Scarred Dragon Archfiend counts as Red Dragon Archfiend** on the field and in the GY, so Earthbound Immortal Red Nova can send it. The Crimson King does not count.
**Most Resonator effects lock your Extra Deck** to DARK Synchros or DARK Dragon Synchros for the turn. The whole Red Dragon family fits. The Fusions, S:P Little Knight, TY-PHON and Chengying do not.
**King's Sarcophagus** sends a Horus monster from your Deck to the GY by sending 1 card from your hand, up to 4 times a turn. It doesn't Summon or draw by itself.
**Stone Sweeper only Summons itself while a card is in a Field Zone.** Chicken Game is your only Field Spell (Crimson Gaia is a Continuous Spell). Its discard effect works any time.
**Red Rising Dragon's GY effect has no targets here.** It needs two Level 1 Resonators in the GY and the deck has none. Play it for its first effect: it revives a Resonator when Synchro Summoned.

str: Ten cards lead to Soul Resonator, and it is a one-card combo.
Abyss negates, The Crimson King punishes monster effects, and Scarred wipes Attack Position monsters.
Red Nova Dragon arrives at Quick Effect speed on either turn.
The Horus engine is a complete second plan that ignores the Resonator locks.
weak: The Resonator locks shut off the generic Extra Deck on combo turns.
One copy each of Red Dragon Archfiend, Darkness Resonator and Power Vice Dragon.
Red Dragon Archfiend destroys your own monsters in the End Phase if they didn't attack.
Horus cards and Level 12s can clog a hand that has no starter.

combos.h: Line A — Soul Resonator into Crimson King and Abyss
combos.about: A one-card combo. Soul Resonator finds Bone Archfiend, and their Levels (3 + 5) make The Crimson King. The King finds Power Vice Dragon, which finds Darkness Resonator, and those two make Scarred. Crimson Gaia adds a Vision Resonator, Darkness lowers it to Level 1, and Scarred + Vision becomes Abyss.

steps.t: **Normal Summon Soul Resonator.** It adds Bone Archfiend from your Deck.
Send 1 other card from your hand (here Nibiru) to the GY to **Special Summon Bone Archfiend**.
Bone Archfiend's effect: send Vision Resonator from your Deck to the GY and make Bone Level 5. Vision **adds Crimson Gaia**.
**Synchro Summon The Crimson King** (Level 8) using Soul (3, Tuner) + Bone (5). It adds Power Vice Dragon.
All your monsters are DARK Synchros: **Special Summon Power Vice Dragon**. It adds Darkness Resonator.
Reveal Red Dragon Archfiend in your Extra Deck to **Special Summon Darkness Resonator** from your hand.
**Activate Crimson Gaia.** Its effect adds your second Vision Resonator from the Deck.
A Level 5+ DARK monster is on the field: **Special Summon Vision Resonator** from your hand.
Darkness Resonator's effect: target Vision Resonator and **change its Level to 1**.
**Synchro Summon Scarred Dragon Archfiend** (Level 8) using Darkness (3, Tuner) + Power Vice (5).
**Synchro Summon Abyss** (Level 9) using Vision (now Level 1, Tuner) + Scarred (8).

end.t: The Crimson King + Abyss + Crimson Gaia. Abyss negates 1 face-up card as a Quick Effect. When they activate a monster effect, the King banishes itself to Summon Red Dragon Archfiend at 6000 ATK, safe from destruction by effects. Soul Resonator in your GY can be banished to save a card from being destroyed.

rules: **Going second:** when Scarred is used for Abyss in step 11, use its effect. It Summons Red Dragon Archfiend and destroys all their Attack Position monsters, and you attack with three Dragons.
Going first, skip that effect. Red Dragon Archfiend would destroy your other monsters in the End Phase.
Every Extra Deck monster here is a DARK Dragon Synchro, so all four locks are satisfied.

combos.h: Line B — Red Nova Dragon on their turn
combos.about: Earthbound Immortal Red Nova is a Quick Effect from your hand or GY. It sends a Red Dragon Archfiend you control to the GY and Summons Red Nova Dragon in its place. Scarred counts as Red Dragon Archfiend, and being sent to the GY triggers Scarred, so you get the real Red Dragon Archfiend as well.

steps.t: Play Line A up to step 10 and stop: you control **The Crimson King + Scarred**. In step 2, send Red Nova as Bone Archfiend's cost.
Their Main Phase, Quick Effect: **banish Red Nova from your GY** and send Scarred (named Red Dragon Archfiend) from your field to the GY.
Red Nova's effect continues: **Special Summon Red Nova Dragon** from your Extra Deck. This counts as a Synchro Summon.
Scarred was sent from the field to the GY: **Special Summon Red Dragon Archfiend** from your Extra Deck.

end.t: Red Nova Dragon + Red Dragon Archfiend + The Crimson King on their turn. Red Nova Dragon gains 500 ATK for each Tuner in your GY (3 here, so 5000), can't be destroyed by their card effects, and can banish itself to negate an attack.

rules: Red Nova works from your hand in the same way. It is once per turn.
Summoning on their turn avoids Red Dragon Archfiend's End Phase effect, which only happens in **your** End Phase.
Red Dragon Archfiend is now out of the Extra Deck, so The Crimson King's Summon effect has nothing to bring out.

combos.h: Line C — Horus opening
combos.about: The Horus cards work with no Normal Summon and no Extra Deck, so they are the play when Soul Resonator is missing or gets negated. Imsety's cost sends Vision Resonator, which searches Crimson Gaia. King's Sarcophagus sends Hapi, and both Level 8s Summon themselves from the GY.

steps.t: Imsety's effect: send it and Vision Resonator from your hand to the GY. **Add King's Sarcophagus**, then draw 1.
Vision Resonator was sent to the GY: **add Crimson Gaia**.
Activate King's Sarcophagus. Send Bone Archfiend from your hand to the GY to **send Hapi** from your Deck to the GY.
You control King's Sarcophagus: **Special Summon Imsety, then Hapi**, from your GY.
Activate Crimson Gaia and **add Soul Resonator**. Your Normal Summon is still free for Line A.

end.t: Imsety + Hapi + King's Sarcophagus + Crimson Gaia, with Soul Resonator in hand and Bone Archfiend in the GY. Horus monsters can't be destroyed by effects that don't target them, and they return from the GY every turn.

rules: If you continue into Line A, Bone Archfiend Summons itself from the **GY** by sending 1 card.
King's Sarcophagus can send up to 4 times a turn. Each card sent as a cost can be a Resonator piece you want in the GY.
Imsety and Hapi each Summon themselves from the GY once per turn.

combos.h: Going second — Super Polymerization
combos.about: **Super Polymerization** is a Quick-Play Spell: discard 1 card, then Fusion Summon using monsters from **either** field. Neither player can respond to it. Two of their best monsters (or one of theirs and one of yours) become one Fusion Monster on your side. The materials are sent to the GY without being targeted or destroyed, so their protection doesn't help. Pick the Fusion by what the two monsters share:

rows.t: Any 2 monsters with different names. Garura doubles the battle damage it deals and draws you 1 card when it goes to the GY. **Your own pair:** Bone Archfiend + Stone Sweeper (DARK Fiends).
Your opponent can't target Mudragon, or any monster sharing its Attribute, with card effects. **Your own pair:** Imsety (Spellcaster) + Bone Archfiend (Fiend), both DARK.

Gains 1000 ATK when it battles a monster with 2200+ ATK, and can Fusion Summon again after a monster is destroyed by battle. **Your own pair:** Soul Resonator (FIRE) + Bone Archfiend (DARK), both Fiends.

rules: Use it **before** any Resonator effect, or on their turn. The Resonator locks stop Fusion Summons for the rest of that turn.
You choose the Fusion when Super Polymerization resolves, so check each monster's Type and Attribute first.
Imsety is the best discard: it can Summon itself from the GY once King's Sarcophagus is out.

earthbound-resonator.arch: DARK Dragon Synchro combo (Resonator → Red Dragon Archfiend family), with Earthbound Immortal Red Nova as a Level 12 shortcut and an independent Horus/King's Sarcophagus grind engine. Super Polymerization ×3 adds instant-speed removal.

primite-blue-eyes.pitch: A deck about getting **Blue-Eyes White Dragon** onto the field and into the GY, then turning it into something bigger. Level 1 Tuners make it a Level 9 Synchro that negates. Two of them make a Rank 8 that negates their whole field. The **Primite** cards add a second engine that Summons Blue-Eyes straight from the Deck.

plan.first: Sage with Eyes of Blue becomes **Blue-Eyes Spirit Dragon** with a Blue-Eyes White Dragon and True Light beside it. On their turn Spirit Dragon negates a GY effect, then Tributes itself for **Ultimate Spirit Dragon**, which negates a card on the field.
plan.second: Lightning Storm or Majesty of the White Dragons clears the way. Then two Blue-Eyes overlay into **Indigo-Eyes Silver Dragon**, which negates every face-up card they control, or **Tyrant Dragon** attacks all their monsters.
plan.win: 3000 to 4000 ATK Dragons. Indigo-Eyes (4000) plus the Blue-Eyes it revives at 4000 ATK is exactly 8000 damage.

open.t: Discard 1 card: add a Level 1 LIGHT Tuner (Sage) **and** a Spell/Trap that mentions Blue-Eyes White Dragon (Roar or True Light).
Normal Summon it to add Maiden of White. It then Links into Spirit with Eyes of Blue.
Normal Summon it to Set Primite Lordly Lode from the Deck. Lode then Summons Blue-Eyes from the Deck.
Adds a Primite card when activated, and Summons a Normal Monster you name from hand, Deck or GY.
Reveal 3 Blue-Eyes cards from your Deck and your opponent picks 1 at random for you. Choose 3 you'd be happy with.

stops: **Ash Blossom.** It answers Wishes, Sage, Bingo Machine and Lordly Lode. The Blue-Eyes and Primite engines start separately, so lead with one and keep the other in reserve.
**True Light leaving the field.** If the face-up True Light is sent to the GY, all your monsters are destroyed. Protect it, or don't place it against decks with lots of Spell/Trap removal.

**Your own restrictions.** While Spirit with Eyes of Blue is on the field you can only Special Summon Dragons. After Lordly Lode's Summon effect, Special Summoned monsters on the field can't activate effects that turn.

engines.t: Level 1 LIGHT Tuners and the Spells that find them. Their job is to put a Blue-Eyes White Dragon in the GY and bring it back, because Tuner (1) + Blue-Eyes (8) is a Level 9 Synchro.

key.t: Normal Summoned: add a Level 1 LIGHT Tuner. From hand: discard it to send your Effect Monster to the GY and Summon a Blue-Eyes monster from the Deck.
Send it from hand or field to place True Light face-up. It Summons itself from the GY when you Special Summon Blue-Eyes White Dragon.
Link-1 made from Sage or Maiden. Adds Mausoleum of White. Tribute it to Summon a Blue-Eyes monster from hand or GY.
Field Spell. One extra Normal Summon for a Level 1 LIGHT Tuner, and it sends a Normal Monster from your Deck to the GY.
Continuous Trap. Each turn: Summon Blue-Eyes White Dragon from hand or GY, or Set a Blue-Eyes Spell/Trap from the Deck. Blue-Eyes White Dragon can't be targeted.
Search Spell. From the GY it equips a Blue-Eyes Fusion from the Extra Deck to your Blue-Eyes White Dragon.
Summons Blue-Eyes White Dragon from Deck, GY or banishment. From the GY it Fusion Summons.
Level 4 Tuner. Summons itself if you control Blue-Eyes White Dragon, and can change a LIGHT Tuner's Level by 1.

engines.t: A small engine for Normal Monsters, and Blue-Eyes White Dragon is one. It needs only the Normal Summon and leaves a negate Set.

key.t: Normal Summoned: Set a Primite Spell/Trap from the Deck. Tribute it to send a Normal Monster from the Deck to the GY. Returns to your hand in your Standby Phase.
Continuous Spell. Adds a Primite card. Name a Normal Monster and Summon it from hand, Deck or GY in Defense Position. Normal and Primite monsters gain ATK.
Quick-Play Spell. Negate and banish 1 face-up card. Free to use while you control a Normal Monster, and it Sets itself again from the GY.

engines.t: Everything here is made from Blue-Eyes White Dragon. Which one you make depends on whether you want protection for their turn or damage on yours.

key.t: Level 9 Synchro. Negates 1 GY effect per turn, and nobody can Special Summon 2+ monsters at once. Tribute it on either turn to Summon another LIGHT Dragon Synchro.
Level 12 Synchro. Quick Effect: negate the activation of a card or effect on the field. Usually Summoned by Spirit Dragon's Tribute effect.
Rank 8 Xyz from 2 Level 8 Dragons. Xyz Summoned: negate all face-up cards they control. Detach to revive a Normal Monster with +1000 ATK.
Level 8 Fusion. Unaffected by Traps and attacks every monster they control. Summoned by Tributing a Blue-Eyes equipped with a Fusion Monster.
Level 9 Synchro. Special Summoned: destroy Spells/Traps, 1 plus the number of Normal Monsters in your GY.
Level 12 Synchro. Adds Synchro Rumble. Quick Effect: target Ultimate Spirit Dragon to swap Crimson Dragon for Stardust Sifr Divine Dragon.

engines.t: **Lightning Storm** ×2 and **Majesty of the White Dragons** (destroy 1 card per Blue-Eyes White Dragon you show, up to 3) clear a board. Infinite Impermanence ×3, Ash Blossom ×3, Ghost Ogre and Droll interrupt. **Synchro Rumble** revives a Tuner or a Level 7-8 Dragon Synchro.

facts.t: **Spirit with Eyes of Blue stops you Special Summoning anything but Dragons** while it is on the field. Maiden of White is a Spellcaster, so she can't return from the GY until Spirit is Tributed.
**Maiden places True Light face-up.** If that face-up True Light is later sent to the GY, every monster you control is destroyed.
**Lordly Lode's Summon effect stops effects of Special Summoned monsters on the field** for the rest of the turn, yours included. Use it last, or not at all on a turn you want Indigo-Eyes' negate.
**Tyrant Dragon needs no Fusion Spell.** Wishes for Eyes of Blue, banished from the GY, equips Neo Blue-Eyes Ultimate Dragon to a Blue-Eyes White Dragon. Tribute that Blue-Eyes to Summon Tyrant.
**Stardust Sifr must be Synchro Summoned.** Crimson Dragon's swap counts as a Synchro Summon, so that works. Spirit Dragon's Tribute effect does not, so it can't Summon Sifr.
**Mausoleum of White doesn't mention Blue-Eyes White Dragon**, so Wishes, Bingo Machine and True Light can't find it. Only Spirit with Eyes of Blue does.
**Indigo-Eyes can only attack directly while it has a Normal Monster as material.** Keep one Blue-Eyes attached.

str: Two separate starting engines: the Eyes of Blue Tuners and Primite.
Spirit Dragon into Ultimate Spirit Dragon gives two negates from one monster.
Indigo-Eyes negates an entire field and sets up exactly 8000 damage.
Lightning Storm ×2, Majesty and Primite Drillbeam ×2 for going second.
weak: Ash Blossom hits almost every starter.
Removing True Light destroys your own board.
Three Blue-Eyes White Dragons in the Deck are bad draws without a way to discard or Summon them.
Several of your own cards restrict what you can Summon or activate that turn.

combos.h: Line A — Sage into Blue-Eyes Spirit Dragon
combos.about: One Normal Summon. Sage finds Maiden and becomes the Link Monster Spirit, which finds the Field Spell Mausoleum. Mausoleum lets you Normal Summon Maiden as well and sends a Blue-Eyes to the GY. Maiden places True Light. Spirit Tributes itself to revive Blue-Eyes, Maiden returns, and the two make Spirit Dragon.

steps.t: **Normal Summon Sage.** It adds Maiden of White from your Deck.
**Link Summon Spirit with Eyes of Blue** using Sage. It adds Mausoleum of White. Activate Mausoleum.
Mausoleum gives an extra Normal Summon for a Level 1 LIGHT Tuner: **Normal Summon Maiden**.
Mausoleum's effect: target Spirit and **send Blue-Eyes White Dragon** from your Deck to the GY.
Maiden's effect: send her from the field to the GY and **place True Light** face-up from your Deck.
Tribute Spirit with Eyes of Blue: **Special Summon Blue-Eyes** from your GY. Maiden then Special Summons herself from the GY.
**Synchro Summon Blue-Eyes Spirit Dragon** (Level 9) using Maiden (1, Tuner) + Blue-Eyes (8).
True Light's effect: **Special Summon Blue-Eyes** from your GY.

end.t: Spirit Dragon + Blue-Eyes White Dragon + True Light. Spirit Dragon negates one GY effect each turn. Then, on their turn, Tribute it to Summon **Ultimate Spirit Dragon**, which negates one card or effect activated on the field. They can't target Blue-Eyes White Dragon while True Light is face-up.

rules: Tribute Spirit with Eyes of Blue **before** Maiden needs to return. While Spirit is on the field you can only Special Summon Dragons.
The monster Spirit Dragon Summons is destroyed in the End Phase. When Ultimate Spirit Dragon is destroyed, it revives a LIGHT Dragon from your GY.
Wishes for Eyes of Blue starts this line too: it adds Sage plus True Light or Roar.

combos.h: Line B — Primite opening
combos.about: The second engine, using only the Normal Summon. Ether Beryl Sets Lordly Lode from the Deck. Lode searches Drillbeam and then Summons Blue-Eyes White Dragon straight from the Deck. With a Normal Monster on the field, Drillbeam needs nothing revealed: it negates and banishes a card on their turn.

steps.t: **Normal Summon Ether Beryl.** It Sets Primite Lordly Lode from your Deck.
**Activate Lordly Lode**: add Primite Drillbeam from your Deck.
Lode's effect: name Blue-Eyes White Dragon and **Special Summon it from your Deck** in Defense Position.
Tribute Ether Beryl: **send a second Blue-Eyes** from your Deck to the GY. (Beryl was Normal Summoned, so Lode's restriction doesn't stop it.)
**Set Primite Drillbeam.**

end.t: Blue-Eyes White Dragon (3300 ATK with Lode) + Lordly Lode + a Set Drillbeam, with a second Blue-Eyes in the GY. On their turn Drillbeam negates and banishes 1 face-up card. In your Standby Phase, Ether Beryl returns to your hand.

rules: After Lode's Summon effect, Special Summoned monsters on the field can't activate effects this turn. Finish Line A first if you have both.
Drillbeam can Set itself from the GY in your Main Phase while you control a Primite monster.
The Blue-Eyes in the GY is ready for True Light, Spirit with Eyes of Blue or Indigo-Eyes next turn.

combos.h: Line C — Tyrant Dragon (going second)
combos.about: A Fusion boss with no Fusion Spell. Wishes finds Sage and Roar, and Roar Summons Blue-Eyes from the Deck. Wishes then works a second time from the GY: it equips a Fusion Monster to Blue-Eyes. A Blue-Eyes equipped with a Fusion can be Tributed for Tyrant Dragon, which attacks every monster they control.

steps.t: Activate Wishes: discard 1 card (here Droll) and **add Sage and Roar of the Blue-Eyed Dragons**.
Activate Roar: **Special Summon Blue-Eyes White Dragon** from your Deck in Defense Position.
Banish Wishes from your GY: **equip Neo Blue-Eyes Ultimate Dragon** from your Extra Deck to Blue-Eyes.
Tribute that Blue-Eyes to **Special Summon Blue-Eyes Tyrant Dragon** from your Extra Deck.
**Normal Summon Sage** and add Maiden of White for next turn.
**Tyrant Dragon (3400 ATK) attacks each of their monsters once.** After it battles, it Sets a Trap from your GY.

end.t: Tyrant Dragon has attacked every monster they control and is unaffected by their Traps. You keep Maiden in hand and Sage on the field.

rules: Roar only lets you Special Summon Dragons from the Extra Deck this turn. Tyrant is a Dragon.
Wishes' search and its GY effect are separate effects, so both work in the same turn.
